mainEntity.name: What is a bump-out addition and how does it differ from a standard room addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bump-out addition is a micro-addition that extends an exterior wall outward, typically by two to three feet, to expand an existing room without building a full-foundation room addition. Common applications include creating space for a kitchen island, adding a soaking tub or double vanity in a bathroom, or building a breakfast nook. Because bump-outs are often cantilevered or set on simple piers, they require less framing and foundation work than a traditional ground-up room. However, they still require structural framing adjustments, exterior modifications, and complete interior drywall finishing. The right approach depends on floor joist direction and setback boundaries.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bump-out extends an exterior wall by a few feet without adding an entire full-sized room, providing targeted interior space for kitchens or bathrooms at a smaller structural scale.
